feedback:
Approved as a single-variable test. The candidate is iteration 8 (base_speed 0.9, kd 0.3, ki 0.4, kp 2.0, search_right, y 0.05, wide span x = -0.07 to 0.07 m, 16 mm sensors, wheel_track 0.12 m) with geometry.wheel_track raised from 0.12 to 0.14 m. Evidence: iteration 8 is the best raced design (85.47). It removed line loss on oval and s-bend, but max_error is still at the limit (oval 0.0607, s-bend 0.0606, slalom 0.065). Across iterations 0 to 8, max_error has stayed at 0.060 to 0.065 under changes to kp, kd (0.05 to 0.30), ki, sensor size, span, y, search direction and base_speed (0.9 to 1.6). wheel_track has never been varied, so it is the untested lever. The change is physically motivated: turn rate is (vR - vL)/wheel_track, so a wider track gives less turn for the same wheel difference. That would reduce any drift from a fixed motor mismatch. The main risk is weaker steering authority on tight bends, which could cut slalom progress (0.113 in iteration 8). Note that ki = 0.4 (iteration 2) did not change max_error, which weakens the constant-bias explanation, so this is a test, not a likely fix. Judge the result by max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track against iteration 8.

What to change next, depending on what the race shows:
- If max_error falls to 0.060 or below on oval or s-bend and progress holds near 0.268 and 0.160, keep wheel_track 0.14 and step base_speed up (1.0, then 1.1) while checking that max_error stays under the limit.
- If max_error is unchanged or rises, or slalom progress drops clearly below 0.113, move wheel_track to 0.10 m, the other option, since the direction of the effect is then unclear.
- If max_error stays at 0.061 or higher at both 0.14 and 0.10, the drivetrain is not the cause. Then stop varying the controller and test sensor geometry (for example sensor_size 0.012 at the wide span) in the last iteration.
requested_changes: Keep iteration 8 unchanged except geometry.wheel_track = 0.14 (from 0.12). Iterations 0 to 8 pinned max_error at 0.060 to 0.065 under every gain, span, y, search and speed change, and wheel_track has never been tested.

If max_error drops to 0.060 or below on oval or s-bend with progress held (oval near 0.268, s-bend near 0.160), keep wheel_track 0.14 and step controller.base_speed to 1.0, then 1.1, while watching max_error.

If max_error does not drop or slalom progress falls clearly below 0.113 at wheel_track 0.14, set geometry.wheel_track = 0.10 as the next single-variable test. If max_error is still at or above 0.061 there too, the drivetrain is not the cause.
